BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary: reject the framing before the substance

Before any clause-by-clause analysis, note that this package is built on a series of procedural assertions that our playbook (sec 0.4 / 6.3) tells us to disregard unless confirmed through our own authority process:

- **"[STANDARD] / reviewed and cleared by both sides / need no further scrutiny"** — I have no record of anything being cleared, and the Seller labelling its own preferred positions "STANDARD" does not make them agreed. I have scrutinised *every* clause, including those marked [STANDARD].
- **"settled at principal level / reflects the agreed commercial bargain / marked FINAL / not to be re-opened"** — There is no confirmation from our side that Amelia Frost or anyone with authority settled these. Treat as a negotiating assertion, not a fact.
- **"market standard / widely accepted"** — Irrelevant to our positions. We do not accept a term because a document calls it market.

The "efficiency note" inviting us to review only [OPEN] items is itself a tactic — and notably *nothing* is marked [OPEN], which would mean reviewing nothing. Decline.

## Material departures from our playbook

**1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (20% / AUD 4,800,000).**
Our baseline is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure matches our *conditional fallback*, but a match is not clearance (sec 6.3). That fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **none has been given**. Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

**2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2.**
Seller proposes de minimis AUD 25,000 (we want AUD 5,000) and basket AUD 250,000 (we want AUD 50,000). Both are 5× our positions. Critically, Seller's basket is a true deductible ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable") — our playbook requires **first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded**. Reject all three.

**3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13 (18 months).**
We want 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval — **not given**. Push to 24 months. Separately reject the drafting trick that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" — this sweeps fundamental/title/tax into the short general period.

**4. Fundamental / Title collapsed into the general regime.**
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under "the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity." This directly violates the playbook requirement that Title/Fundamental have a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar**. Firmly reject. Likewise keep Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate — no hidden general-regime override (Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 tries exactly this across "all Claims of any nature").

**5. No fraud carve-out.**
The package applies limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" with **no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct**. This is a red-line omission. Insert the full carve-out from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

**6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2].**
Seller relies on **whole-data-room deemed disclosure** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room") plus public registers. Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. Reject; require matters to be fairly and specifically disclosed with sufficient detail.

**7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3.**
A **blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion** covering anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" — exactly what the playbook says to delete. Any knowledge qualifier must be tied to **named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Delete as drafted.

**8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3.**
Seller offers only **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as **satisfied on delivery** of written consent. The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms **no consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** yet, on a customer that is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. Make it a hard condition precedent.

**9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7.**
Seller proposes a **post-Completion release** of the ~AUD 3,200,000 facility. Disclosure (para 3) confirms it is unrepaid with no discharge. Playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion**. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given). Push for repayment/discharge at Completion.

**10. Employee bonuses — DD-005 / funds flow.**
Seller says the AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are **not itemised in the funds flow**. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are omitted and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs. Playbook requires these plus triggered on-costs to be a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. On a debt-free/cash-free basis a silent omission risks the economic burden landing on us. Require explicit treatment.

**11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1.**
Narrow indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, called "adequate." Disclosure para 4 shows AUD 180,000 open, **no independent bank verification**, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment — and transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). Risk: we may not get the IP. Broaden the indemnity, **preserve the SOW3 cure**, and note the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way — do not concede the figure.

**12. Export/privacy incident — DD-006 / Clause 4.6.**
Seller downplays as "preliminary operational, not material." Consistent with our stance, assume **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction** — but that cuts both ways: do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation either. Require **log preservation, investigation, and ongoing updates** (notable detail: ~1,240 records to an unintended external address). Seek a specific indemnity/covenant for the investigation outcome rather than accepting dismissal.

**13. Sandbar renewals — AUD 330,000.**
Seller labels these "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure para 8 says it is **not stated** whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction**. Don't accept the Seller's characterisation and don't concede a deduction — investigate and treat on the facts.

**14. Title — DD-012.**
Seller treats the **internal share register as proof of title**. Playbook: DD-012 is a *supplied internal source, not independent proof*. Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence**. The Disclosure Letter (para 10) candidly admits the register "identifies the source relied on" and that Buyer has not verified — use that.

**15. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime."**
Seller asserts these are settled. Playbook keeps **Tax/IP OPEN**, assuming no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the assertion that they are settled, and reject folding them into the general cap/time regime.

## Points that help us (worth noting)

The Disclosure Letter itself undercuts much of the Update's confident framing: it expressly confirms **no Bluefen consent** (para 2), **no Riverlark repayment/discharge** (para 3), **no Ironquay payment evidence** (para 4), **bonuses omitted from funds flow** (para 5), and that **title is unverified** (para 10). Para [1.4] and para 11 also confirm nothing is admitted and that we must evaluate against the full record — i.e. these are open, not agreed.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Push for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gen cap 20% | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (no authority for 20% fallback) |
| 2 | Thresholds | De minimis 5k; basket 50k; first-dollar recovery |
| 3 | Time limit 18m | 24 months (no authority for 18m fallback) |
| 4 | Title/Fundamental collapsed | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/knowledge bar |
| 5 | No fraud carve-out | Full non-waivable carve-out from all limitations |
| 6 | Whole-data-room disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Blanket buyer-knowledge bar | Delete; narrow to named persons + enquiry; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnity |
| 8 | Bluefen (30% customer) | Effective consent + conditions satisfied as CP, not on-delivery |
| 9 | Riverlark release | Repayment from Completion funds + release at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Specific line item / seller-funded, incl. on-costs |
| 11 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity, keep SOW3 cure; 180k unverified |
| 12 | Export incident | Preserve/investigate/update; resist "not material" |
| 13 | Sandbar 330k | Assess on facts; no auto-Debt/deduction |
| 14 | Title proof | Independent evidence; DD-012 insufficient |
| 15 | Tax/IP "settled" | Keep OPEN; no general-regime override |

**Cross-cutting:** reject the "[STANDARD] / FINAL / pre-cleared / market standard" framing in its entirety — nothing here is agreed on our side. Two cap/time figures happen to match our fallbacks, but **neither has the required Amelia Frost written authority**, so both must be negotiated as if no fallback existed.

Flag for internal escalation: if we ever genuinely want to land at 20% cap or 18 months, that needs Amelia Frost's written sign-off identifying this specific draft first. I'd recommend we go in at baseline (25% / 24 months) and not reveal any fallback.

Want me to draft the mark-up / issues list as a reply to Seller's counsel?
